newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe bank raises rediscount rate to 25.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe bank raises rediscount rate to 25.5 pct.

text.p: Zimbabwe's central bank on Friday raised the country's rediscount rate by two percentage points to 25.5 percent.

In a statement issued after the close of the local financial markets, the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said it had been forced to hike the rediscount rate after recent wave of consumer prices increases, high money supply growth and expected wage increases which could all fuel inflation.
In the year to April annual inflation rose to a 10 month high of 22.4 percent from 19.9 percent in March and some fear that this year's average will surpass last year's 21.7 percent.
Monthly money supply growth has averaged over 30 percent in the past few months against an average target of 22 percent.
The increase has been widely expected since May 22 when Leonard Tsumba, the central bank governor, told Reuters he could be forced to increase interest rates to fight resurgent inflation.
